# Jubilees Chapter 27 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Esau's fury; Rebekah sends Jacob away

---

**27:1** And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and he said in his heart: "The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will slay Jacob my brother."

**27:2** And the words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah, and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him: "Behold, Esau thy brother is comforting himself concerning thee by planning to kill thee.

**27:3** And now, my son, hearken to my voice, and arise and flee to Laban my brother in Haran.

**27:4** And dwell with him for some days until thy brother's wrath turns away, and the anger of thy brother turns from thee, and he forget what thou hast done to him, and I will send and bring thee from thence. Why should I be bereft of you both in one day?"

**27:5** And Rebekah went and said to Isaac: "I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth, such as these — from the daughters of the land — what good is my life to me?"

**27:6** And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and charged him, and said to him: "Thou shalt not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

**27:7** Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father, and take thee a wife from thence from the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother.

**27:8** And God Almighty bless thee and make thee fruitful and multiply thee, and thou shalt become a company of peoples.

**27:9** And may he give to thee the blessing of Abraham my father, to thee and to thy seed after thee — that thou mayest inherit the land of thy sojournings which God gave to Abraham."

**27:10** And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah the mother of Jacob and Esau.

**27:11** And when Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram to take himself a wife from thence, and that in blessing him he had charged him, saying: "Thou shalt not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"

**27:12** And that Jacob had hearkened to his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram;

**27:13** And when Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were evil in the eyes of Isaac his father,

**27:14** Then Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife, in addition to the wives he already had.

**27:15** And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba and went toward Haran. And he came upon a certain place and lodged there, for the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.

**27:16** And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God were ascending and descending upon it.

**27:17** And behold the LORD stood above it and said: "I am the LORD the God of Abraham thy father and the God of Isaac. The land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it and to thy seed.

**27:18** And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south. And in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

**27:19** And behold I am with thee, and will keep thee wherever thou goest, and will bring thee back to this land. For I will not leave thee until I have done that which I have spoken to thee."

**27:20** And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said: "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I knew it not."

**27:21** And he was afraid and said: "How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."

**27:22** And Jacob rose early in the morning and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up as a pillar-stone, and poured oil upon the top of it.

**27:23** And he called the name of that place Beth-El. But the name of the city was Luz at the first.

**27:24** And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: "If God be with me and keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on,

**27:25** And I come back in peace to my father's house, then shall the LORD be my God.

**27:26** And this stone which I have set up as a pillar-stone shall be God's house; and of all that thou givest me I will surely give the tenth to thee."

---

*EMET notes: Chapter 27 covers the parallel to Genesis 27:41–28:22. The Ge'ez expands Isaac's second blessing (vv.8-9). "Pillar-stone" renders the Ge'ez term for massebah. The ladder vision follows the Ge'ez closely with minor expansions over MT Genesis 28:12-19.*
